about: Places to go further than this guide does: explanations drawn by hand, videos, and pages that run a model in front of you so you can watch what it does. Every one is somebody else's work, chosen because it made something clearer.
The list is picked, not gathered, so it is short on purpose and will grow. Each link was checked on the date above, and each opens in a new tab.

sections.heading: Reference
sections.about: Writing that explains one idea thoroughly, with the pictures to go with it.

sections.heading: Videos
sections.about: Explanations that move, for when an idea is easier watched than read.

sections.heading: Visualisers
sections.about: Pages that run or draw a real model, so you can see each step happen.

links.title: The Illustrated Transformer
links.about: The transformer drawn one step at a time, from a single word's vector through self-attention and many heads to the decoder. Still the gentlest way in to the diagrams every later explanation borrows.

links.title: How DeepSeek Rewrote the Transformer [MLA]
links.about: How multi-head latent attention shrinks the memory a model keeps for every token it has read, and why that let DeepSeek serve long contexts cheaply.

links.title: Transformer Explainer
links.by: Polo Club of Data Science, Georgia Tech
links.about: GPT-2 small running in the browser. Type a prompt and watch it become tokens, attention and a choice of next word, with temperature and sampling to play with.

links.title: LLM Visualization
links.about: A model drawn in three dimensions, every weight and sum in place, walked through one layer at a time from a tiny nano-GPT up to the scale of GPT-3.
